title: Visiting the Sheldrick Trust Nairobi Nursery

facts.fact: The nursery rescues and rehabilitates orphaned elephants and rhinos in Nairobi National Park; reintegration into the wild is its stated aim.
facts.evidenceExcerpt: The SWT Nursery, located in Nairobi National Park, is where an orphan's journey begins

facts.fact: Public nursery visits require advance booking and an official SWT confirmation; same-day reservations are not accepted.
facts.evidenceExcerpt: Access to the Nursery is strictly by advance booking only. ... It is not possible to make same-day bookings

facts.fact: Park entry payable to KWS is separate from the nursery entry donation, including for visitors not taking a game drive.
facts.evidenceExcerpt: regardless of whether they will venture further into Nairobi National Park or not

facts.fact: Only keepers may feed and directly interact with the elephants.
facts.evidenceExcerpt: only Keepers are allowed to feed and directly interact with them

facts.fact: Nairobi National Park hosts rhinos, lions, leopards, buffaloes, giraffes and zebras; sightings are not guaranteed.
facts.evidenceExcerpt: home to rhinos, lions, leopards, buffaloes, giraffes, zebras and so much more!

facts.fact: The nursery entrance is KWS Mbagathi/Workshop Gate on Magadi Road.
facts.evidenceExcerpt: Access to the orphanage is via the KWS Mbagathi Gate, also known as the KWS Workshop Gate, on Magadi Road

notes: Read captured official operator/institution page. Only listed stable facts and explicitly reviewed booking/payment rules used. Transient details should be rechecked with operator before travel. All advisory itinerary choices are editorial recommendations, not operator guarantees.
